key_insight: Video diffusion quality is limited less by how sparse attention is, and more by whether the sparse mask matches the geometric structure of full attention. Veda exploits this by distilling an attention pattern that preserves quality even at high sparsity.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the quadratic self-attention bottleneck that makes high-resolution, long-video generation with Diffusion Transformers slow and memory-intensive. It also addresses the quality drop seen in existing sparse attention methods when sparsity becomes too aggressive.
method: Formulates sparse tile selection as an explicit distillation problem, learning which attention tiles matter most.
Aligns sparse masks with the tile-wise geometry of full attention instead of using generic sparsity patterns.
Uses distilled sparse attention to reduce computation while maintaining generation quality at high sparsity levels.
impact: Veda makes long-video diffusion more scalable, enabling higher-resolution and longer temporal outputs with lower compute cost. For practitioners, this suggests a practical path to efficient video generation without the usual quality trade-off from sparse attention.
